question: In a spinal (subarachnoid) block, local anaesthetic is deposited within the dural sac, directly bathing the nerve roots in cerebrospinal fluid, whereas in an epidural block, it is deposited in the potential space outside the dura.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Re-read the anatomy section. The subarachnoid (intrathecal) space lies inside the dural sac and contains CSF. The epidural space is outside the dura, between dura and ligamentum flavum.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This anatomical distinction is fundamental: spinal LA mixes with CSF (rapid onset, predictable spread); epidural LA diffuses through the dura and around nerve roots (slower onset, segmental, volume-dependent).
